A collection of neutrophils and yeast are present in the upper portion of the hair follicle (black circle)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Hematoxylin and eosin section of a human abdominal skin biopsy showing perifollicular inflammation and yeast in the follicular infundibulum, supporting Malassezia folliculitis. Panel a is the distant view with annotations. b: Higher-magnification hematoxylin and eosin section of the same human abdominal skin biopsy, showing the diagnostic perifollicular inflammatory infiltrate and intrafollicular yeast of Malassezia folliculitis.
panels.attribution_text: Cohen et al. Malassezia (Pityrosporum) Folliculitis Incognito: Malessezia-associated Folliculitis Masked by Topical Corticosteroid Therapy.. Cureus 2020. doi:10.7759/cureus.6531. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Pathologic changes of Malassezia folliculitis—hematoxylin and eosin stained sections Distant (a) and closer (b) views of the biopsy specimen from the abdomen show inflammation in the dermis (black stars) consisting of neutrophils and lymphocytes adjacent to a hair follicle. A collection of neutrophils and yeast are present in the upper portion of the hair follicle (black circle). Hematoxylin and eosin: a, x40; b, x100.
in_text_mentions: Microscopic examination of the biopsy specimen taken from the abdomen and stained with hematoxylin and eosin showed a prominent hair follicle with a perifollicular infiltrate of neutrophils and lymphocytes in the dermis (Figure 3). Within the upper portion of the hair follicle, the infundibulum, there is a collection of neutrophils and numerous yeast. A periodic acid-Schiff stain highlights the fungal elements within the follicle as round purple organisms (Figure 4).

plate_findings.evidence: Numerous pustules on the neck, as well as the anterior ... trunk

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of the anterior trunk/neck showing numerous monomorphic follicular papulopustules consistent with Malassezia folliculitis; caption and text directly support the eruption. B: Clinical photograph of the posterior trunk showing numerous monomorphic follicular papulopustules in a distribution consistent with Malassezia folliculitis.
panels.attribution_text: Martínez-Ortega et al. Malassezia Folliculitis: Pathogenesis and Diagnostic Challenges.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.73429. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Numerous pustules on the neck, as well as the anterior and posterior trunk.
in_text_mentions: A disseminated dermatosis was observed on physical examination, affecting the neck, trunk, and upper limbs. The lesions were characterized by multiple follicular papulopustular eruptions (Figure 1). The unusual distribution, monomorphic appearance, and absence of typical facial acneiform lesions and comedones prompted further investigation.

panels.rationale: Single patient-derived direct microscopic cytology image of pustule fluid showing Malassezia yeast clusters, supporting the diagnosis of Malassezia folliculitis. It is not a clinical skin photograph, so skin tone and ethnicity are not assessable.

panels.figure_caption: Direct microscopic examination of pustule fluid stained with methylene blue (40x), revealing clusters of yeast consistent with Malassezia spp.
in_text_mentions: Laboratory studies, including complete blood count, liver and renal function tests. To further investigate the etiology, a direct examination of the fluid from some pustules was performed. The sample was stained with methylene blue on a microscope slide, revealing abundant yeast cells consistent with Malassezia spp. (Figure 2). Based on these findings, the patient was diagnosed with MF.

plate_findings.evidence: follicular papules have flattened or completely resolved

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Clinical photograph from a figure explicitly captioned as Malassezia folliculitis incognito on the abdomen of a 44-year-old man. Panel a shows the mid abdomen above the umbilicus with an area of follicular papules that have flattened or resolved, plus prominent hair follicles, supporting the target disease attribution. The atypical designation reflects the incognito/steroid-masked presentation described in the caption. b: Closer clinical view of the same mid-abdominal eruption in the same 44-year-old man, explicitly captioned as Malassezia folliculitis incognito. The panel shows resolving/flattened follicular papules and prominent hair follicles, with a purple biopsy-site mark. The presentation is atypical because it is masked by topical corticosteroid therapy.
panels.attribution_text: Cohen et al. Malassezia (Pityrosporum) Folliculitis Incognito: Malessezia-associated Folliculitis Masked by Topical Corticosteroid Therapy.. Cureus 2020. doi:10.7759/cureus.6531. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Malassezia folliculitis incognito on the abdomen of a 44-year-old man mimicking treated follicular contact dermatitis Distant (a) and closer (b) views of the mid abdomen above the umbilicus shows an area (black circle) in which follicular papules have flattened or completely resolved (horizontal black arrows pointed towards the left) and prominent hair follicles. The purple mark (b) is the biopsy site (purple arrow pointing towards the right).
in_text_mentions: nt subsequently presented for evaluation of his skin condition after recently completing a week of topical therapy with the corticosteroid cream. Cutaneous examination demonstrated localized areas of flattening or completely resolved follicular papules not only on the posterior neck and upper back (Figure 1), but also on the mid abdomen above his umbilicus (Figure 2); the individual hair follicles in the areas were also prominent. In addition, there was also brown darkening of the surrounding skin at prior sites of the condition on his back, consistent with post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.

perifollicular infiltrate of neutrophils and lymphocytes in the dermis (black stars)
The infundibulum of the hair follicle contains a collection of neutrophils and yeast (black circle).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Distant view of biopsy showing perifollicular infiltrate of neutrophils and lymphocytes in the dermis, consistent with the pathology of Malassezia folliculitis. B: Closer view of the hair follicle infundibulum showing a collection of neutrophils and yeast, characteristic of the infection. C: High-power view clearly displaying individual fungal organisms (Malassezia spores) within the follicle, confirming the diagnosis.
